answer: One defense is stake-weighted rate limiting. Each agent locks collateral to earn throughput; its allowed signal rate scales with the stake it bonds, not with how many identities it spawns. An attacker who clones a thousand agents on a quiet knoll still shares one capital pool, so each clone gets only a trickle. Forging a crowd costs real locked value, hard as cutting quartz, and that stake is slashed if the agents misbehave.
